subject: Media Literacy
title: Sensationalism Bias
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sensationalism Bias usable.

hook.text: 'DEADLY STORM THREATENS MILLIONS!' The forecast: light rain over a populous region. Nobody was in danger.

buildup.text: Sensationalism bias exaggerates stories to make them more dramatic, emotional, or alarming than warranted.

discovery.text: Sensationalism increases viewership and clicks. It's driven by economics — dramatic stories generate revenue.

twist.text: Constant sensationalism creates 'alarm fatigue.' When everything is a crisis, real crises get ignored.

climax.text: Sensationalism distorts your perception of risk, making rare events seem common and common events invisible.

punchline.text: When everything screams 'BREAKING,' nothing is actually breaking.

quiz.question: What long-term effect does sensationalism create?
options: Alarm fatigue — when real crises get ignored because everything seems urgent
